title: Belfast & Donegal
standfirst: Belfast maritime material, Raphoe legal and property records, and a Killybegs account preserve distinct Glasgow occurrences. They are not a reconstructed founder family.
question: Do any contemporary records connect the Belfast and Donegal people to one another or to Antrim?
answer: No reviewed record supplies a father–son, collateral or identity bridge. Captain James at Belfast, Thomas in the Raphoe district and James in a Killybegs account must remain separate documentary clusters until a source names a relationship.

chapters.title: A Belfast shipmaster
body: PRONI maritime material identifies Captain James Glasgow or Glascow as a Belfast-associated shipmaster active by 1667. In 1669/70, James Glasco, mariner, was admitted and sworn a free commoner of Belfast.
A 1686 Belfast will extract is a lead for further reading, not a proved death date; no inspected source names James's parents, spouse or children.

chapters.title: Thomas in the Raphoe legal network
body: Thomas Glasgow appears in a Raphoe-linked court case in 1684, at Lifford in the 1689 attainder list, and in Ballindrait and Shannon property transactions from 1692 to 1695.
A 1701 Exchequer entry is a high-confidence continuation. These records show a documented adult actor, not his birth, family or beneficial ownership of every property named.

evidence.label: State of the Protestants of Ireland

chapters.title: A Killybegs account occurrence
body: A parliamentary table lists James Glasgow in Killybegs collector-account material under 1728.
The accounting date is not his birth or death date, and no record joins him to Thomas or Captain James.

chapters.title: Three settings, no pedigree
body: Thomas and the Killybegs James are an adjacent-generation Donegal comparison, not a proved relationship. Belfast and east Antrim share a regional corridor, but the evidence does not identify Captain James with the Kilwaughter householder.
Each cluster needs its own original records before any connection can be claimed.

clusters.title: Captain James of Belfast
clusters.summary: A shipmaster and free commoner occurrence is securely associated with Belfast.
clusters.boundary: The will extract has not been read for relatives or date type, and no family is established.

clusters.title: Thomas in Raphoe, Ballindrait and Shannon
clusters.summary: Court, attainder and deed evidence supports a continuing adult Donegal actor.
clusters.boundary: The records do not state his birth, spouse, children or relationship to other Glasgows.

clusters.title: James in Killybegs accounts
clusters.summary: The parliamentary table places James in collector-account material.
clusters.boundary: It is not a death record and names no kin.

clusters.title: Unproved regional comparisons
clusters.summary: Geography and chronology provide research leads only.
clusters.boundary: No source connects the three settings or attaches them to Kilwaughter.

links.label: Adjacent-generation Donegal comparison without stated kinship
No bridge to east Antrim or Donegal

proved: Captain James was a Belfast maritime actor.
Thomas was active in Raphoe-linked legal and property records.
A Killybegs account names James under 1728.
supported: Thomas's records form a high-confidence continuing Donegal identity through 1701.
hypothesis: Thomas and the Killybegs James may be related across an adjacent generation.
unresolved: Any parent-child, collateral or identity bridge between Belfast, Raphoe and Killybegs.

gaps.title: Read the Belfast will extract and maritime records
gaps.why: They may name Captain James's associates or relatives and clarify the 1686 date.

gaps.title: Trace Thomas through probate and Betham material
gaps.why: A probate or family record could resolve his origins and succession.

gaps.title: Identify the Killybegs collector record
gaps.why: The underlying account may clarify James's role and associates.
